description: Introduce a pluggable rendering-engine abstraction in tools/render.py so the engine is selectable instead of hardcoded to Chromium/agent-browser. Keep the existing agent-browser (Chromium) path working as one engine, add a WeasyPrint engine (in-process, via the `weasyprint` library), and design an extensible registry so more engines can be added. Make the engine selectable by CLI flag, environment variable, and Makefile variable, following the repo's existing patterns. This aligns the real code with the two-engine design already documented in README.md's 'Rendering engine' section.
steps: In tools/render.py, refactor the HTML-building portion (Jinja2 environment setup, fixture load, assets wiring, writing work/<level>/<key>/rendered.html) into a reusable helper (e.g. build_html(level, report_key) -> (html_str, work_dir, destination)). This HTML generation must be identical regardless of engine, so both engines render the same input.

Define an engine abstraction: a small protocol/base with a `name` and a `render(html_path_or_str, pdf_path, base_url, work_dir) -> None` method, plus a registry dict mapping engine name -> engine implementation. Keep it simple and extensible (adding an engine = registering one class/callable).

Implement `ChromiumEngine` (name 'chromium') that preserves the CURRENT behavior exactly: shells `agent-browser --session <session> open <uri>` / `wait 1000` / `pdf <path>` / `close`, runs with cwd=ROOT, always closes the session in a finally block, and raises RuntimeError if the output does not start with b'%PDF-'. Do not change the snap-confinement-safe working directory behavior (writes happen under the project tree).

Implement `WeasyPrintEngine` (name 'weasyprint') that renders in-process: `from weasyprint import HTML; HTML(string=html, base_url=<source_dir>/).write_pdf(pdf_path)`. base_url must point at the template source dir so relative font/css url() references resolve (verified working during routing: council_best_students renders to a valid 4-page 792x612 PDF).

Choose the default engine. Chromium remains the documented house default for CSS fidelity (README says 'the house default'), so default to 'chromium' UNLESS routing/FEAT-003 shows WeasyPrint meets the same fidelity gates broadly; keep the default as chromium and make weasyprint opt-in. Wire selection precedence: explicit CLI flag > MUSSANNONI_ENGINE env var > default. Read the env var in the render entrypoint.

Update `render(level, report_key, *, engine=None)` to resolve the engine (arg -> env var -> default), build the HTML once, and dispatch to the selected engine. Keep the existing public signature backward compatible (engine defaults to None/chromium) so `from tools.render import render` in tools/convert.py keeps working; also thread an optional engine param through convert.convert / convert_all if straightforward, defaulting to the same resolution.
Update tools/render.py argparse to add `--engine {chromium,weasyprint}` (choices derived from the registry so new engines appear automatically). Print the chosen engine alongside the output path.

Update tools/doctor.py: agent-browser is only required for the chromium engine and weasyprint for its engine. Report each engine's availability (agent-browser on PATH; `import weasyprint` succeeds) without failing the whole doctor when only one engine is present. pdftoppm stays required (it is the comparison rasteriser, engine-independent).

Update tools/compare.py: replace the hardcoded report.json field "engine": "chromium (headless, print-to-pdf)" (~line 382) so the recorded engine reflects what actually produced rendered.pdf. Simplest correct approach: accept the engine name as a parameter to compare()/pass it through convert, and write that. If threading it is awkward, record the engine used at render time into a small sidecar (e.g. output/.../render-meta.json) that compare reads. Do NOT change any THRESHOLDS or metric logic.

Update the Makefile: add an `ENGINE ?=` variable and pass it through to the render/convert invocations (e.g. `uv run python -m tools.convert ... $(if $(ENGINE),--engine $(ENGINE),)` and similarly for a render target if one is added). Keep existing targets working with no ENGINE set (defaults to chromium).

Update README.md 'Rendering engine' section and docs if needed so the documented engines match the real CLI/flags (README currently references a nonexistent mussannoni/pdf.py; describe tools/render.py --engine, the env var, and the Makefile ENGINE variable instead). Do not overclaim WeasyPrint fidelity; state that a pass on one engine is a separate verification from the other, consistent with existing README wording.

Add/extend tests in tests/ for the abstraction: a test that the engine registry exposes both 'chromium' and 'weasyprint'; a test that engine selection resolves arg > env var > default; and a test that WeasyPrintEngine actually produces a valid multi-page %PDF- for at least one real template (e.g. render primary council_best_students via the weasyprint engine into a tmp path and assert page_count and b'%PDF-' header via pymupdf). Skip the chromium-engine execution test if agent-browser is unavailable, but still unit-test that ChromiumEngine builds the correct agent-browser command list. Keep ruff clean.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students --engine weasyprint` produces a valid output/primary/council-best-students/rendered.pdf (starts with %PDF-, 4 pages, page size 792x612 pt).
`uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students --engine chromium` still works exactly as before (or is skipped only if agent-browser is genuinely unavailable, documented in findings).
`MUSSANNONI_ENGINE=weasyprint uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students` (no flag) selects weasyprint; an explicit --engine flag overrides the env var.
`from tools.render import render` continues to work unchanged for tools/convert.py (default engine preserved).
report.json's engine field reflects the engine that actually produced the render, not a hardcoded string.
`make convert-one LEVEL=primary REPORT=council_best_students ENGINE=weasyprint` runs the full loop with WeasyPrint.
New tests pass and `uv run ruff check .` is clean.
No THRESHOLDS in tools/compare.py or tests/test_fidelity.py were changed; corpus/ untouched.
verification: uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students --engine weasyprint
uv run python -c "import pymupdf,sys; d=pymupdf.open('output/primary/council-best-students/rendered.pdf'); print(d.page_count, d[0].rect); assert d.page_count==4"
findings:
Implemented a pluggable rendering-engine abstraction in tools/render.py. Split HTML generation into build_html(level, report_key) -> (html, work_dir, destination, base_url) so both engines render identical input; a post-render optimize hook (FEAT-003) can run cleanly after any engine writes rendered.pdf. Added an Engine Protocol (name + render(**kw) keyword-only, including a `session` string) and an ENGINES registry dict. ChromiumEngine (name 'chromium') preserves the exact original behaviour: same agent-browser open/wait 1000/pdf/close command list (extracted into build_commands for unit testing), cwd=ROOT, finally-block close, RuntimeError if output is not %PDF-, session name kept as 'render-<level>-<key-dashes>'. WeasyPrintEngine (name 'weasyprint') renders in-process via `from weasyprint import HTML; HTML(string=html, base_url=<source_dir>/).write_pdf(path)` (import kept lazy inside render so the chromium path never imports weasyprint). Selection precedence arg > MUSSANNONI_ENGINE env var > default 'chromium' via resolve_engine(); render(level, report_key, *, engine=None) stays backward compatible for tools/convert.py. convert.convert/convert_all and their argparse gained an optional --engine threaded through (choices from engine_names()). render.py argparse gained --engine with choices derived from the registry and prints 'engine: path'.

Engine recording: render() writes output/<level>/<key>/render-meta.json {"engine": name}; compare.py's new render_engine() reads that sidecar and maps to a label (chromium -> 'chromium (headless, print-to-pdf)', weasyprint -> 'weasyprint (in-process)'), replacing the hardcoded report.json engine string. No sidecar (existing committed reports) falls back to the historical chromium label so committed report.json values are unaffected. THRESHOLDS and all metric logic untouched.

doctor.py: REQUIRED_BINARIES reduced to ('pdftoppm',) (engine-independent rasteriser, still required). New engine_report() reports chromium (agent-browser on PATH) and weasyprint (import succeeds) each with ok/-- but does NOT fail the whole doctor when only one engine is present; it only requires that at least one engine is usable. Verified doctor still prints 'environment ready' with both present.

Makefile: added ENGINE ?= and threaded $(if $(ENGINE),--engine $(ENGINE),) into convert/convert-secondary/convert-primary/convert-one; added a new `render` target. No ENGINE set defaults to chromium (verified via make -n). README 'Rendering engine' section rewritten to describe tools/render.py --engine, MUSSANNONI_ENGINE, and Makefile ENGINE (removed the nonexistent mussannoni/pdf.py reference); kept the 'pass on one engine is not a pass on the other' wording.

Tests: tests/test_engine.py covers registry exposes both engines, default is chromium, names match, selection arg>env>default incl. unknown-engine ValueError, ChromiumEngine.build_commands exact command list (no agent-browser execution needed), build_html engine-independence, and WeasyPrintEngine rendering primary/council_best_students into a tmp destination (monkeypatched output_dir so committed output/ is untouched) asserting %PDF-, 4 pages, 792x612, and the weasyprint render-meta sidecar. Chromium execution test omitted (build_commands unit-tested instead) per the spec's allowance.

Verification: `uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students --engine weasyprint` -> valid 4-page 792x612 PDF; chromium engine still renders valid 4-page PDF; MUSSANNONI_ENGINE=weasyprint selects weasyprint and --engine overrides it; `make convert-one LEVEL=primary REPORT=council_best_students ENGINE=weasyprint` ran the full loop and report.json recorded 'weasyprint (in-process)'. `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run pytest` 664 passed, 46 skipped (was 654/46; +10 new tests). All committed output/, catalog/reports.yaml, and template calibration.json/fixture.json touched by verification runs were restored via git checkout; the working tree contains only the intended source/test/doc changes plus the FEAT-001 pyproject/uv.lock weasyprint dependency. Note: WeasyPrint fidelity is NOT gated here (its layout differs from Chromium); a weasyprint render of council_best_students measured worst_ssim 0.9857 which is below the 0.98 SSIM... actually above 0.98 but pixel_delta 2.21% exceeds the 0.5% gate, so it is 'wip' under chromium-tuned thresholds - consistent with the README note that engine fidelity is separately verified.
